title: Build and optimize surface models
action: Construct the two slab models: Pd‑CeO₂ (rhombohedral Pd₄ cluster on CeO₂(111)) and Pd‑iC‑CeO₂ (four C–H species inserted at the interface). Optimize geometries with DFT (PBE+U, D3 dispersion) until forces converge. Ensure the correct Ce³⁺ reduction pattern (one Ce³⁺ in Pd‑CeO₂, five Ce³⁺ in Pd‑iC‑CeO₂).
description: Prepare the starting geometries for all subsequent calculations. The agent must build these models from scratch using the slab setup parameters given in the paper.

title: CH₄ activation barrier calculation
action: Adsorb CH₄ on both optimized surfaces, then locate the transition state for the first C–H bond breaking (CH₄* → CH₃* + H*) using the climbing‑image nudged elastic band (CI‑NEB) method. Compute the activation energy E_act = E(TS) − E(initial state).
description: This step produces the activation energy for methane dissociation, which is the rate‑limiting step on Pd‑iC‑CeO₂. The resulting barriers are directly comparable to the paper's reported values.

title: H₂O₂ adsorption and decomposition to OH*
action: Adsorb H₂O₂ on both surfaces and decompose it to 2OH* species. Record the relaxed co‑adsorbed OH structures for use in the Eley–Rideal mechanism.
description: Generate the surface OH* groups required for the Eley–Rideal initial states. The structures are needed as input for step_04.

title: Eley–Rideal‑like pathway barriers for methanol formation
action: Set up the initial states: on Pd‑iC‑CeO₂, co‑adsorb CH₃*, H*, and 2OH*; on Pd‑CeO₂, co‑adsorb CH₃*, 2OH*, and OH_int*. Introduce the 8H₂O·2OH(aq) complex. Use CI‑NEB to determine the reaction paths for (i) formation of CH₂OH* and (ii) formation of CH₃OH(aq) on each catalyst. Report the activation barriers.
description: This is the key computational claim of the paper. The barriers for CH₂OH and CH₃OH formation via the solvated Eley–Rideal mechanism are reported and compared between the two catalysts.
